# Shiba Inu volume surge slows after 12x rally

Shiba Inu volume spiked nearly 12-fold during Sunday's 36% price jump, fueling one of the strongest daily rallies the memecoin has seen in months. But the momentum is already showing cracks. Trading activity has cooled significantly since the initial surge, and traders are now watching whether SHIB can hold key support near $0.00000500.

The volume explosion on Sunday was remarkable. Daily trading volume jumped close to $380 million — the highest in months — as SHIB added roughly $1 billion to its market cap in a single session, pushing the price to approximately $0.0000057. That kind of move with zero news catalyst is almost textbook memecoin behavior. No product announcement. No team update. Just sudden buying pressure hitting all at once.

### What drove the surge?

South Korean traders were the primary engine. The SHIB/KRW pair on Upbit accounted for roughly $62 million in volume during the rally — over 10% of global SHIB trading from a single exchange and currency pair. The pair also traded at a slight premium compared to Binance and other platforms, pointing to concentrated regional demand pressure. The timing aligned with late Saturday and Asian morning hours, consistent with Korean retail flow patterns.

Around $6 million worth of SHIB positions got liquidated during the surge, hitting roughly 2,300 traders. Most were short positions, and the damage concentrated during the single most intense hour of trading. The liquidations followed the price increase — they amplified the move but didn't cause it.

### Exchange outflows signal holder confidence

More than 1 trillion SHIB tokens have been withdrawn from centralized exchanges in recent weeks. Exchange outflows reduce the supply immediately available for sale, and while they don't guarantee higher prices, they often signal that investors prefer to hold rather than trade.

Burn activity has also accelerated. According to Shibburn, over 1 trillion SHIB were permanently removed from circulation during the recent rally — the largest burn in roughly a year. The increase coincided with Woofswap DEX v3 launch, whose ecosystem mechanisms contribute additional burns through platform activity.
